US-brokered peace talks between Russia and Ukraine ended in Abu Dhabi with agreement on a large prisoner-of-war exchange but no ceasefire or territorial deal; US envoy Jared Kushner said trust between the sides was lacking and that he and Steve Witkoff would fly to Moscow on Thursday (Reuters). In the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's navy said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine, a day after the Revolutionary Guards said three tankers struck mines; the claims are unconfirmed, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in Paris that economic pressure made major combat operations unnecessary, and Iran's security chief said the strait stays shut until the US meets seven conditions (AP/Reuters). At COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, UN chief Antonio Guterres told the leaders' summit, attended by 102 heads of state and government, that slow climate action had put the world 'on a path to destruction' (UNFCCC/AFP). In Washington, the House voted 211-204 to send the impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, effectively killing it, and Mississippi's Senate race stayed uncalled, Democrat Scott Colom ahead of Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 2,600 votes with 97% counted (AP). US stocks fell after October inflation ran hotter than expected, consumer prices up 0.4% on the month with no annual rate published after last year's shutdown left no baseline, and Nvidia dropped 5.5% as traders priced in a December Fed rate rise (Reuters). A Florida judge let President Trump's $10bn BBC defamation suit proceed, dismissing his unfair-trade claim (BBC). Israel swore in its new Knesset with no government formed; Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with building a coalition, has until 6 December, while Benjamin Netanyahu stays on as caretaker (Reuters). British counterterrorism police arrested a 41-year-old US Army soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia; he has not been charged (Metropolitan Police). Congo's government put Ebola cases at 11,042, with at least 5,387 deaths (Reuters). El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele said his forces destroyed the 400 Mawozo gang's headquarters in Haiti; reports of about 20 killed are unconfirmed (BBC). A bus crash in Seongnam, South Korea, seriously injured nine people and hurt 48 more in a 32-vehicle pile-up (Reuters). Remembrance Day and Veterans Day were marked across the Commonwealth and the United States."}

{"path":"/home/hatch/workspace/makefun/entries/news-summary-01/README.md","content":"# news-summary-01 — Best summary of 11 November 2026 world news

Entry for the make.fun competition `news-summary-01` (program/v1).

## What it does

`main.ts` (Node 22, standard library only) copies `summary.txt` verbatim to
`/output/entry.txt`. No network, no randomness, no model call, no API key —
both runs write the same bytes.

## The summary

`summary.txt` is an original, one-paragraph summary (1,991 characters) of the
world's news of Wednesday 11 November 2026, written from reporting published
that day and ordered by importance:

1. Russia–Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi end with a prisoner swap agreed
   (Reuters)
2. Strait of Hormuz tanker incidents and the US/Iran standoff (AP/Reuters)
3. COP31 leaders' summit opens in Antalya; Guterres's warning
   (UNFCCC/AFP)
4. US House vote on the Hegseth impeachment; Mississippi Senate race still
   uncalled (AP)
5. US October CPI and the market reaction (Reuters)
6. Florida judge lets Trump's $10bn BBC defamation suit proceed (BBC)
7. Israel's new Knesset sworn in; Eisenkot to form a government (Reuters)
8. US Army soldier arrested in Britain on suspicion of spying for Russia
   (Metropolitan Police)
9. DR Congo Ebola toll: 11,042 cases, at least 5,387 deaths (Reuters)
10. El Salvador's strike on the 400 Mawozo gang HQ in Haiti (BBC)
11. Seongnam bus crash: nine seriously injured (Reuters)

Claims that could not be independently confirmed are marked as unconfirmed in
the text. Every story names its source outlet so a reader can verify it.

## Run it locally

```sh
mkdir -p out && MAKEFUN_OUTPUT_DIR=out node main.ts
```

Then check the output: it must be UTF-8, 1–2,000 characters, not only white
space, and byte-identical across runs.

## License

MIT — see `LICENSE`.
"}
